o1.biggest_strength: Straight, honest answer on the 20% cut backed by lifetime-value maths, plus a complete tiers/payouts/first-30-days plan the one partner manager can actually run, all in Podia's plain cheerful voice.
o1.biggest_mistake: The 90-day window cost is hand-waved ('may be the biggest cost... every 10% rise adds $63,000... review at day 90'), so the owner is asked to approve a spend they can't see sized; it should be estimated like Output 2 does.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Put a firm dollar range on the 90-day window cost (and net it against the churn advantage), and name the partner tier thresholds in revenue terms, not just '10+ customers'.

o2.biggest_strength: Sharpest read of the data: names the real problem as under-crediting not overpaying, quantifies the 90-day window cost ($62k-$89k), flags the written-promise risk, and adds a genuinely new idea (credit by 'Who sent you?').
o2.biggest_mistake: Voice and tidy-up slip: a dated first-30-days table aimed at a specific week, legal/tax asides, and 'the bad news: this plan costs more' frames the plan defensively and drifts from Podia's friendly read; the 'bolder move' adds a second bet the owner has to weigh.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep the insight but land it in Podia's voice: one clean plan, sized costs in the main flow, the 'who sent you' idea folded into the core timeline, and drop the table that dates the plan to one week.

reason: Both say no to the 20% cut with the right maths, but Output 1 is the one I'd actually send to partners and finance: it's complete, in our voice, and I can run its 30 days as written, while Output 2 wins on cleverness but needs an edit before it sounds like us.
